name: Ålesund
title: Ålesund Hull Thickness Measurement | Fishing, Cruise, Offshore
description: Hull thickness measurement in Ålesund for fishing vessels, offshore vessels, cruise ships and coastal cargo ships: tank, hold, deck and piping UTM alongside.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Fishing Fleets, Offshore Vessels and Cruise Ships in Ålesund
intro: Ålesund, the art nouveau town spread over the islands of Sunnmøre, is the commercial centre of a coast that lives from fishing, offshore shipping and shipbuilding, and its harbour also receives cruise ships bound for the Geirangerfjord. Pelagic trawlers, offshore vessels, coastal cargo ships and the coastal express all call, and the yards around the town dock vessels from across the region. When a ship needs gauging here, our technicians fly from India to Ålesund and go straight to the vessel.

highlights.h: Pelagic trawlers and their RSW tanks
highlights.p: The ocean-going pelagic fleet of this coast carries its catch in refrigerated seawater tanks that are filled, emptied and cleaned season after season. Coating damage in those tanks leads to rapid wastage and pitting, and between fishing seasons they can be gauged alongside.

highlights.h: Cruise ships bound for the fjords
highlights.p: Cruise ships call at Ålesund on their way to and from the Geirangerfjord. A day call rarely allows tank entry, but machinery-space piping, scrubber lines and accessible deck structure can be measured when the operator plans for it with the agent.

Many owners of supply, anchor-handling and construction vessels are based along the Sunnmøre coast, and their vessels return to regional yards for dockings. Pre-docking gauging during a stay at Ålesund gives the yard a steel estimate before the dock date arrives.

port.h: Ålesund's harbours, fishing fleet and seasonal traffic
p: Ålesund is built across several islands at the outer edge of the Sunnmøre archipelago, between the sounds that lead in from the open sea and the long Storfjorden system that reaches inland to Geiranger. Its position on the coastal shipping lane, close to rich fishing grounds, made it a fishing and fish-export town long before the oil industry arrived, and klippfisk, cod salted and dried for markets in southern Europe and South America, is still produced and traded here. The town centre was rebuilt in art nouveau style after the fire of 1904, and the old harbour in the middle of town now serves mainly cruise ships, the coastal express and smaller craft, while cargo work has moved to terminals around the islands.

The working port is spread around the islands and the mainland opposite. Container and general cargo quays handle feed, fish exports and supplies, and coastal tankers and bulk carriers bring fuel and building materials. The fishing fleet based on this coast is among the largest in Norway: ocean-going pelagic trawlers and purse seiners, whitefish trawlers and longliners land catches and maintain their vessels here. Offshore shipowners from the surrounding municipalities run supply, subsea and anchor-handling vessels that return to the region between contracts. Through the summer, cruise ships call frequently, many of them continuing into the Geirangerfjord, which is a World Heritage site, and the coastal express calls daily in both directions.

Ships stay in Ålesund for very different lengths of time depending on the trade, and gauging is planned to match. Fishing vessels lie alongside between seasons, sometimes for weeks, which is the best window for fish holds, refrigerated tanks and piping. Offshore vessels in port between contracts, or waiting for a yard slot, can open ballast tanks and chain lockers. Cruise ships and the coastal express keep tight schedules and allow only limited work. Weather is the main constraint: Ålesund faces the Norwegian Sea north of Stad, and autumn and winter storms are frequent, although the sounds and harbours inside the islands give the shelter that deck work needs on most days.

facilities.h: Quays, yards and waiting positions around Ålesund
p: Gauging in the town itself is done at the fishing and commercial quays, at the cargo terminals and on the cruise and coastal express berths during calls. A fishing vessel tied up between seasons can have its tanks pumped out and ventilated by the crew, and the quays give easy access for equipment. Cargo ships discharging at the terminals offer shorter windows, suited to deck, hatch coaming and accessible tank work. Ships waiting in the sounds for a berth or a yard are reached by boat, which the agent arranges.

For dockings, the region has a dense ring of shipyards. Vard, headquartered in Ålesund, runs yards in the surrounding municipalities; the yards at Ulsteinvik are a short ferry crossing away; and repair yards on the nearby islands, such as Fiskerstrand Verft at Sula, dock ferries, fishing vessels and offshore vessels. Which yard a vessel uses is the owner's choice, and the team travels to it. Readings taken at an Ålesund quay can form the first stage of a programme completed in dock.
list: Fishing and commercial quays — fish hold, RSW tank and seawater piping gauging on trawlers and purse seiners between seasons.
Cargo terminals — deck, hatch coaming and ballast tank readings on coastal cargo ships and bulk carriers during discharge.
Cruise and coastal express berths — machinery-space piping and scrubber line measurements during calls, planned with the operator.
Offshore vessel lay-by berths — ballast tank, chain locker and deck gauging on supply and anchor-handling vessels between contracts.
Regional repair yards, including Fiskerstrand Verft at Sula — docking and renewal-survey gauging on ferries, fishing and offshore vessels.
Waiting positions inside the islands — short jobs by boat on vessels waiting for a berth or a yard slot.

context.h: Fjord emission rules, fishing regulation and port state control
p: Ålesund lies north of 62°N and therefore outside the North Sea emission control area, but Norway's own rules reach into the fjords the cruise ships visit. The country is phasing in zero-emission requirements for ships in its World Heritage fjords, the Geirangerfjord among them, starting with smaller passenger ships, and cruise operators have been adapting fleets and itineraries accordingly. For the older cruise ships that still call here, scrubber systems and their wash-water piping remain a maintenance priority. Port state control on foreign-flag ships is the responsibility of the Norwegian Maritime Authority, working within the Paris MoU.

The fishing fleet is overwhelmingly Norwegian-flagged. Norwegian fishing vessels are surveyed under the Norwegian Maritime Authority's rules, with much of the survey work carried out by classification societies on its behalf, and the larger ocean-going vessels are classed. Pelagic trawlers built during earlier rounds of fleet renewal are now old enough for steel condition to drive repair decisions, and when such vessels change hands, pre-purchase gauging protects the buyer. Engine and propulsion upgrades supported by Norway's NOx Fund have been common across this fleet, and upgrade dockings are often the moment owners choose to have hull and tank condition measured too.

jobs.h: Gauging jobs in Ålesund through the year
jobs.p: The calendar in Ålesund follows the fishing seasons and the offshore market. Pelagic vessels come in between the herring, mackerel and blue whiting seasons, offshore vessels between contracts, and cruise ships through the summer. Most requests are focused: a set of tanks, a piping system or a deck area that a surveyor or superintendent wants measured, sometimes as preparation for a docking at one of the region's yards. Larger renewal-survey programmes are usually carried out in dock, and our team travels to the yard for those. Pre-purchase work tends to come at short notice, when a vessel is about to change hands. Examples:
list: A pelagic trawler between seasons: RSW tank plating and stiffeners gauged, with pitting depths recorded where the coating has broken down.
A cruise ship on a summer call: scrubber wash-water and overboard pipework measured with the system shut down, results reported before departure.
An anchor-handling vessel between contracts: ballast tanks and chain lockers measured as a pre-docking estimate for a regional yard.
A coastal general cargo ship discharging at a terminal: hold, tank top and hatch coaming readings for the owner's condition file.
A whitefish trawler offered for sale: pre-purchase gauging of shell, fish hold and double bottom tanks for the prospective buyer.

logistics: Ålesund Airport, Vigra, lies on an island north-west of the town and is linked to it by subsea road tunnels; it has frequent flights to Oslo and Bergen as well as some international routes. Port access is arranged by the vessel's agent, and work at the regional yards by the yard on the owner's request. Norway is in the Schengen area, so technicians coming from India need Schengen visas; for fishing vessels whose port stays follow the season, early notice of the expected lay-up dates lets visas be arranged in time.

faqs.q: Can RSW tanks on a fishing vessel be gauged in Ålesund?
faqs.a: Yes, when the vessel is alongside between seasons and the tanks have been emptied, cleaned and ventilated. RSW tanks are coated and usually insulated on the shell side, and wastage tends to start where the coating has broken down, so we combine gauging with a close look for pitting and record depths where we find it. The owner gets readings tied to the tank drawings before the next season begins.

faqs.q: Is it possible to gauge a cruise ship during an Ålesund call?
faqs.a: Within limits. A day call does not allow tanks to be emptied and entered, but scrubber piping, machinery-space pipework and accessible deck structure can be measured if the operator plans the work with the agent and the system concerned can be shut down. For a larger scope, the better window is a technical stop or the ship's next docking.

faqs.q: Which yards near Ålesund dock offshore and fishing vessels?
faqs.a: The region has many: Vard's yards in the surrounding municipalities, the yards at Ulsteinvik and repair yards on the islands near the town, among others. The owner chooses the yard by slot and capability, and our team goes to whichever one has the vessel. Readings taken at an Ålesund quay beforehand can serve as the pre-docking steel estimate.

faqs.q: How do autumn storms affect work in Ålesund?
faqs.a: They affect boat transfers and open-deck work more than anything else. Inside the harbours the shelter is good, and tanks, holds and machinery spaces can be worked in almost any weather. Jobs on ships waiting in the sounds, reached by boat, are the ones most likely to be postponed, so we keep a quayside fallback in the plan whenever we can.

faqs.q: Can pre-purchase gauging be arranged at short notice in Ålesund?
faqs.a: Usually, provided the team's visas are valid and the seller allows access. Pre-purchase work on a fishing or offshore vessel lying in Ålesund focuses on the areas that drive repair decisions: shell plating near the waterline, double bottom tanks, holds and the most corrosion-prone tanks. The buyer's adviser sets the priorities, and the report is laid out so it can support the negotiation.
